recipes.name: New York-Style Bagel Recipe

ingredients.name: bread flour or high gluten flour (you may need up to 1/2 cup / 60g for kneading)

instructions: In 120ml of the warm water, pour in the sugar and yeast. Do not stir. Let it sit for five minutes, and then stir the yeast and sugar mixture until it all dissolves in the water.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Make a well in the middle and pour in the yeast and sugar mixture.

Pour 1/3 cup / 80ml of warm water into the well. Mix and stir in the rest of the water (the scant 1/2 cup / 100ml that is remaining), as needed. Depending on where you live, you may need to add an additional couple tablespoons to about ¼ cup/60ml of water. You want a moist and firm dough after you have mixed it.
On a floured countertop, knead the dough for about 10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. Try working in as much flour as possible to form a firm and stiff dough.

Lightly brush a large bowl with oil and turn the dough to coat. Cover the bowl with a damp dish towel. Let rise in a warm place for 1 hour, until the dough has doubled in size. Punch the dough down, and let it rest for another 10 minutes.

Carefully divide the dough into 8 pieces (I used a scale to be extra precise, but it’s not necessary). Shape each piece into a round. Now, take a dough ball, and press it gently against the countertop (or whatever work surface you’re using) moving your hand and the ball in a circular motion pulling the dough into itself while reducing the pressure on top of the dough slightly until a perfect dough ball forms (as pictured). Repeat with 7 other dough rounds.

Coat a finger in flour, and gently press your finger into the center of each dough ball to form a ring. Stretch the ring to about ⅓ the diameter of the bagel and place on a lightly oiled cookie sheet. Repeat the same step with the remaining dough.
After shaping the bagels and placing them on the cookie sheet, cover with a damp kitchen towel and allow to rest for 10 minutes. Meanwhile, preheat your oven to 425F / 220C / Gas Mark 7.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Reduce the heat. Use a slotted spoon or skimmer to lower the bagels into the water. Boil as many as you are comfortable with boiling. Once the bagels are in, it shouldnt take too long for them to float to the top (a couple seconds). Let them sit there for 1 minute, and then flip them over to boil for another minute. Extend the boiling times to 2 minutes each, if you’d prefer a chewier bagel (results will give you a more New York-Style bagel with this option).

If you want to add toppings to your bagels, do so as you take them out of the water. Alternatively, you can use an egg wash to get the toppings to stick before baking the bagels. You may want to use the Optional Toppings listed above to top the bagels. Use just one topping, or a combination to make your own Everything Bagel Seasoning.
Once all the bagels have boiled (and have been topped with your choice of toppings), transfer them to an oiled or parchment-lined baking sheet.
Bake for 20 - 25 minutes, or until golden brown (I usually err on the side of 20 minutes).
Cool on a wire rack (Or, if you are impatient like I am, slice one of these babies open and spread on some of your favorite cream cheese or softened butter. Take a bite Oh babyyy!)

recipes.name: No-Knead Brioche
instructions: Stir the flour, yeast and salt together in a large bowl.
In a jug, whisk the melted butter, eggs, milk and honey together.
Stir the wet ingredients into the dry with a wooden spoon for about 30 seconds until smooth, with no big lumps. Cover with cling film.
Leave at room temperature for 2 hours.
Press the dough down to knock out the air, cover and refrigerate for at least 12 hours, ideally overnight (up to 48 hours).
Grease a 23 x 13cm loaf tin.
Divide the cold dough in half and roll each piece into a 35cm rope. Pinch the tops together, twist into a braid, tuck the ends under and place in the tin.
Cover and leave to rise for 2-3 hours until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 190C (170C fan). Gently brush the loaf with egg wash.
Bake for 25-30 minutes until deep golden brown, then cool before slicing.

recipes.name: Japanese Sausage Bread (Wiener Pan)
instructions: Put all the dough ingredients into a bread machine and run the dough cycle.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces and rest them for 15 minutes, loosely covered with cling film so they don't dry out.
On a lightly floured surface, flatten each piece into an oval. Spread a thin layer of mustard in the middle if using, and lay a sausage on top.
Make cuts in the dough with a dough scraper, then wrap it snugly around the sausage and pinch the seam firmly so it doesn't open in the oven.
Leave to rise until doubled in size: at room temperature in summer, or about 30 minutes on the oven's proving setting in winter.
Heat the oven to 200C. Squeeze over ketchup and sprinkle with parsley, then bake for about 15 minutes until golden.

recipes.name: Butter French Bread Rolls
instructions: Bread machine: add everything except the butter and start the dough cycle. Add the butter after 7-8 minutes of mixing, let the cycle finish, then skip to step 5.
By hand: make a well in the flour, put the sugar and yeast in the centre and the salt at the edge. Pour in the water and milk warmed to about 35C and mix into a dough.
Knead for 5-10 minutes, then knead in the butter until smooth and shape into a ball.
Cover with a damp cloth and leave to rise. It's ready when a floured fingertip pressed into it leaves a hole that doesn't spring back.
Knock back the dough, divide into 6 pieces, shape loosely and rest for 15 minutes, then shape into rolls.
Leave to prove until nearly doubled, keeping the surface from drying out. Meanwhile heat the oven and a baking sheet to 250C.
Dust with flour, slash the tops and lay a sliver of butter in each cut. Mist with water.
Put in the oven, turn down to 220C and bake for 10 minutes, then lower to 200C for about 5 minutes until golden. Adjust for your oven.
Cool slightly before eating. For a sweeter dough, use 100ml milk and no water, 15g butter and 15g sugar.

recipes.name: Fluffy Butter Rolls

ingredients.name: beaten egg thinned with a little water (for glazing)

instructions: Combine all the dough ingredients in a bowl and knead until smooth.
Cover and leave to rise in the oven on a 35C proving setting for 30 minutes.
Gently knock back, divide into 8 pieces and roll into balls. Cover with a damp cloth and rest for 10 minutes.
Flip each ball, flatten lightly, roll into a log, then roll one end under your palm to make a teardrop shape.
With the thin end towards you, roll the dough away from you with a rolling pin to about 20cm long.
Roll it back up from the wide end, tuck the end underneath and press lightly. Place on a lined baking sheet.
Prove at 35C for about 28 minutes, until 1.5 times bigger.
Heat the oven to 180C. Brush the rolls with the thinned egg (so they don't burn) and bake for 13 minutes until golden.

recipes.name: Basic Baguette

ingredients.name: French T65 flour (or half strong, half plain flour)

instructions: Mix the water and yeast in a bowl.
Add the flour and salt and mix, then knead on the worktop for about 10 minutes until smooth (it doesn't need to be glossy).
Leave to rise somewhere warm (28-30C) for 60 minutes. Knock it back gently, then leave for another 30 minutes. It's ready when a floured fingertip leaves a dent that doesn't spring back.
Divide into two 300g pieces, cover and rest for 15-20 minutes.
Shape each piece into a long baguette.
Prove on a floured cloth (couche), seam side up, at 28-30C for 50-60 minutes.
Heat the oven to 240C.
Roll the loaves onto a baking sheet and dust with strong flour if you like.
Make 3-4 long diagonal slashes along the top of each loaf.
Bake for 15-20 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool on a rack.

recipes.name: Twisted Sugar Doughnuts (Twist Sugar Pan)
instructions: Put all the dough ingredients in a bowl and mix well.

Knead until smooth. Warm a frying pan over a medium heat for 30 seconds, turn off the heat, then put the dough (in its bowl or covered) in the pan and leave for about 30 minutes until clearly puffed up.
Divide the dough into 6 equal pieces and roll each into a smooth ball.
Stretch each piece into a thin rope, fold and twist it. Leave at room temperature for about 20 minutes until slightly risen.
Heat the oil to 160C and fry the twists, turning, until golden brown all over. Drain briefly.
Toss in sugar while still warm.

recipes.name: Honey Milk Nama Shokupan
instructions: Warm the cream to about 30C (and the water too, in winter). Stir the honey into the water until dissolved.
Mix the flour, salt and yeast in a bowl. Add the honey water and cream and fold with a spatula into a shaggy dough.
Turn out and knead until the dough stretches into a thin, see-through film without tearing.
Shape into a ball, cover and leave to rise at 30C for about 1 hour, until a little more than doubled. A floured finger poked in should leave a hole that doesn't spring back.
Divide into 2 or 3 pieces, roll into balls, cover and rest for 15 minutes.
Roll each piece into an oval, fold the sides into the middle, then roll it up and pinch the seam lightly.
Place seam side down in an oiled 1-loaf (about 900g) tin, ideally a lidded Pullman tin.
Prove at 30C in a humid spot for 45-50 minutes, until the dough domes just above the rim.
Heat the oven to 190C and bake for 27-30 minutes, adjusting for your oven.
Turn out and cool on a rack before slicing.

recipes.name: Honey Stick Bread
instructions: Put all the ingredients into a bread machine and run the dough cycle.
Rest the dough for 10 minutes, then roll it out into a rectangle.
Cut into 12 long strips (halve them for shorter sticks) and lay them on a lined baking sheet.
Prove at 40C for 30 minutes (the oven's proving setting works well).
Heat the oven to 170C and bake for 16 minutes until lightly golden. Don't mist with water before baking, so they stay soft and fluffy.

recipes.name: Fluffy Nikuman Dough (Steamed Bun Wrappers)

ingredients.name: skimmed milk powder (or use 60ml water + 80ml milk instead of the water and powder)
filling of your choice (e.g. seasoned pork mince)
soy sauce with vinegar, or mustard, to serve

instructions: Put all the dough ingredients into a bread machine and run the dough cycle (or knead by hand until smooth and leave to rise).
Turn the dough onto a floured surface, divide into 8 equal pieces and roll into balls.
Roll each ball into a flat round and put a spoonful of filling in the middle.
Gather the edges up around the filling, pleating as you go, and pinch firmly at the top to seal.
Place each bun on a square of baking paper and steam over boiling water for 12-15 minutes.
Serve hot, plain or with vinegar-soy sauce or mustard.

recipes.name: Loaf
instructions: Put the flour, water, sugar, salt and yeast into the stand mixer and mix.
Once the dough has come together, add the butter in 3-5 pieces. Mix for another 10 minutes, or until the dough is nicely elastic.
Turn the dough out onto the work surface, shape it into a smooth ball and leave to prove until doubled in size.
Divide into 3 equal pieces. Press out the gas, stretch each piece, fold it into 3, then roll it up into a shape that fits the tin.
Place all 3 pieces side by side in an oiled loaf tin.
Leave to prove again until 1.5 times bigger. When it has risen about 1.2 times, start heating the oven to 180C fan (start earlier if your oven is slow to heat).
Bake at 180C fan for 32 minutes.
Take it out of the tin and leave on a wire rack until completely cool.

recipes.name: Shio butter pan - Salt and butter bread

ingredients.name: butter - for placing inside when rolling
egg - for egg wash: can be milk or oil

instructions: Put the flour, water, sugar, salt and yeast into the stand mixer and mix.
Once the dough has come together, add the butter in 3-5 pieces. Mix for another 10 minutes, or until the dough is nicely elastic.
Turn the dough out onto the work surface, shape it into a smooth ball and leave to prove until doubled in size.
Divide into 12 equal pieces.
Press out the gas, stretch each piece, create isosceles triangle shape.
Place butter piece at the bottom of the triangle, roll towards the tip of the triangle - should look like croissant.
Place them on the baking tray.
Leave to prove again until 1.5 times bigger. When it has risen about 1.2 times, start heating the oven to 180C fan (start earlier if your oven is slow to heat).
Egg wash on each pieces, then sprinkle sea salts
Bake at 200C/180C fan for 11 minutes.
Take it out of the tin and leave on a wire rack

recipes.name: Kalacs - Hungarian sweet marble bread

ingredients.name: raisins - as many as you like

instructions: Separate all dry ingredients for white and cacao parts.
Warm milk up, put all the sweetners and melt them thoroughly.
Pour 230ml of milk into white-dry ingredients, let the stand mixer mix them for 10 minutes or until it gets elastic.
Pour 270ml of milk into cacao-dry ingredients, let the stand mixer mix them for 10 minutes or until it gets elastic. (cacao powder can go all over the place. Start from the slowest setting)
Once both doughs are ready, prove them until double the size.
Place white one on the work surface, roll it out. Them place cacao one on top.
Place raisins where you want them to be.
Make braids out of the combined dough.
Bake at 180C for 32 minutes or longer if needed.
